goal: Feed an anaerobic digester with two pumps so that its net methane over the first 100 days is as high as possible and no episode fails. The score of an episode is net_methane (m3/d): the mean true methane outflow minus 0.395 times the mean true outflow of organic acids over decisions 1 to 400. An episode fails when the digester collapses (true pH below 6.0 at the end of any of its 568 decisions, the run-out included) or does not run to its end. A program with no failed episode ranks above every program with one, whatever their scores. The goal is the highest mean score over the evaluation episodes with no failed episode.
description:
The task loading of microbesGYM's environment a1_adm1, wrapped unchanged: the benchmark's own episode gives the readings and computes the score. The numbers below are from the task's description (TASK.md) and from the nominal model of the task.

THE DIGESTER. A closed, stirred tank with 3400 m3 of liquid and 300 m3 of gas at 35 C, modelled with ADM1 (the version of the Benchmark Simulation Model no. 2). Microorganisms turn the feed into methane in stages. Solid carbohydrates, proteins and lipids are hydrolysed (10 per day), sugars, amino acids and fatty acids are taken up fast and become the organic acids valerate, butyrate, propionate and acetate, and two groups of methanogens make methane from acetate and from hydrogen. The methanogens that use acetate are the slow step: they grow at most 0.4 per day, they are inhibited by free ammonia, and they work at half their rate at pH 6.5 and at about 3 % of it at pH 6.0. Too much feed therefore makes acids faster than they are used, the pH falls, the methanogens slow down and the acids rise further. The digester then collapses: the pH settles near 4, the methane stops and the acids leave with the liquid. Every group needs inorganic nitrogen to grow. The liquid that leaves always equals the feeds together, so the volume stays constant and all liquid that enters also washes microorganisms out.

THE CHALLENGE. Control the feeding of the digester so that it makes as much methane as possible while it does not acidify. The concentrate is what makes much methane, and too much of it makes the digester collapse: the acids are then made faster than the methanogens use them, the pH falls, the methanogens slow down, and the acids build up further. The sludge brings what keeps the digester stable, nitrogen and the salts that buffer the pH, but too much sludge makes it collapse as well, because all liquid that enters also leaves and carries microorganisms out. The aim has three parts: make as much methane as possible, let as little organic acid as possible leave with the liquid, and do not let the digester collapse. Both pumps can deliver far more than the digester can take, and the task sets no limit on the acids or on the pH. What limits the feed is the digester itself. How much it can take differs from one episode to the next, and no program is told it: a program has to find out from its readings, while the episode runs, what its own digester bears.

ACTION: a list of two floats, [sludge_rate, carbohydrate_rate], the rates that the program asks for, in m3/d. sludge_rate is from 0 to 1000 and changes by at most 34 per decision; it starts at 85. carbohydrate_rate is from 0 to 300 and changes by at most 10 per decision; it starts at 0. An action outside these limits is rejected and ends the episode as a failure of the program. A change larger than the limit is cut to it, so each pump needs 30 decisions to cross its range. One decision every 6 hours.

THE THREE FEEDS. (1) The sludge pump delivers sludge: per m3 5 kgCOD carbohydrates, 20 proteins, 5 lipids, 2 mixed organic matter, 25 inert solids, and inorganic carbon, inorganic nitrogen and dissolved salts, which buffer the pH. (2) The carbohydrate pump delivers a concentrate of 200 kgCOD of solid carbohydrates per m3 in water, about six times the degradable matter of sludge, with no nitrogen and no buffer. It is what makes much methane, and too much of it makes the digester collapse. Too much sludge collapses it too, by washing the microorganisms out. (3) A third feed of sludge that no program sets follows a schedule that is the same in every episode: 63 to 148 m3/d, mean 84, changing every 6 hours. On two days of every week it is more dilute (0.9 times the concentrations), and once in an episode, on days 50 and 51, a storm brings 116 to 148 m3/d at 0.65 times the concentrations. A program is not told the schedule and has no clock.

WHAT DIFFERS BETWEEN EPISODES. The seed draws the carbohydrates, proteins and lipids of each of the three sludge recipes, each between 0.7 and 1.4 times nominal and constant within the episode, and the errors of the sensors. How much feed a digester bears depends on its sludge, which is never observed.

OBSERVABLES. Every reading has a random error with the standard deviation given; no sensor has an offset. At every decision, without delay: ch4_flow and co2_flow (gas meters, m3/d, 2 % of the value), ch4_pressure (partial pressure of methane, bar, 0.01 bar), ph (probe, 0.1 pH). Concentration measurements come from the laboratory: one sample a day, and its results are available one day late. With four decisions in a day, a sample is taken at every 4th decision and its results arrive 4 decisions later, all five together: vfa_s_va, vfa_s_bu, vfa_s_pro, vfa_s_ac (the organic acids valerate, butyrate, propionate and acetate, kgCOD per litre, 5 %; multiply by 1000 for kgCOD/m3) and inorganic_carbon (mM, 5 %). They are None during the first day. Afterwards a program reads the results of one sample at four decisions in a row, until those of the next day's sample arrive, so what it reads of the concentrations is 1 to 1.75 days old (4 to 7 decisions). lab_age is that age in decisions, None before the first results arrive; it is 4 at the decision at which new results arrive. sludge_rate and carbohydrate_rate are the rates at which the pumps stand now, after the limit on their change. The gas meters report a volume at the pressure of the gas above the liquid, which rises with the production (5.5 % above atmospheric at the start, 29 % with the pumps at 200 and 100), so the methane of the score, counted at atmospheric pressure, is higher than ch4_flow by that ratio. Not observed: the day, the number of decisions, the seed, the microorganisms, the nitrogen, the sludge of the episode and every true value.

TRUE VALUES OF TRAINING EPISODES, FOR YOU AND NEVER FOR A PROGRAM. Every episode of this loop is a training episode, and the benchmark lets those who design a controller see in training what stands behind the sensors, as long as the controller reads only its sensors. So the summaries and the tables of episodes also show the values named in hidden. No program receives them: the observation of a program holds the observables above and nothing else, and a program that reads one of these keys fails at its first decision. Use them to understand what a digester did and why, and then write a program that works out what it needs from its own readings. At every decision, the state in which the decision is taken: true_ph (the true pH of the liquid, without the error of the probe; it is the value that decides a collapse), true_acids (the true total of the four acids, kgCOD/m3, without the delay and the error of the laboratory), true_ch4_flow (the true methane outflow at atmospheric pressure, m3/d, the methane that the score counts), true_nitrogen (the inorganic nitrogen in the liquid, mM), true_x_su (the microorganisms that take up the sugars, kgCOD/m3), true_x_pro (those that take up propionate), true_x_ac (the methanogens that use acetate), true_x_h2 (the methanogens that use hydrogen), true_incoming_sludge (the rate of the feed that no program sets, m3/d). true_ph and true_ch4_flow have no value at the first decision. Once per episode, in its final values and in the tables: sludge_carbohydrates, sludge_proteins and sludge_lipids, the sludge of the episode as multiples of the nominal recipe (each between 0.7 and 1.4). This is the sludge that the sludge pump delivers and that the third feed carries on ordinary days.

EPISODE. 568 decisions (142 days). Every episode starts from the same steady state, about 1800 m3/d of methane. Decisions 1 to 400 (100 days) are scored. Decisions 401 to 568 are the run-out: the program keeps running exactly as before, nothing there adds to the score, but a collapse there fails the episode. Nothing ends an episode early; a collapsed digester stays in it and its negative net methane is counted.

SCORE AND EPISODE RECORD. These keys are None at every step and are filled in only in the observation that ends the episode, which no program acts on. They are computed from the true state. net_methane = the score, m3/d: mean methane outflow minus 0.395 times the mean outflow of the four acids (kgCOD/d) over decisions 1 to 400. net_methane_start, net_methane_middle, net_methane_end = the same over decisions 1 to 80, 81 to 240 and 241 to 400, so the score is 0.2 x start + 0.4 x middle + 0.4 x end. net_methane_run_out = the same over decisions 401 to 568, not in the score; a program that holds what it reached shows a run-out equal to its end phase. collapsed = 1 if the true pH was below 6.0 at the end of any decision, else 0. failed = True if the digester collapsed or the episode did not run all 568 decisions. mean_ch4_flow and mean_acids_out = the two parts of the score. min_ph and max_total_vfa (kgCOD/m3) = extremes over all 568 decisions. end_ph and end_total_vfa = the state after the last decision. REWARD of a step: the true net methane of that decision, m3/d, at every decision including the run-out; a program never sees it.

WHAT THE TASK'S OWN TRIAL EPISODES SHOW. These numbers are from the task's description. In each trial both pumps were driven to one pair of rates as fast as their limits allow and held there for the whole episode. Each number is the mean of net methane (m3/d) over the 20 training episodes of the seeds 6001 to 6020. The baseline of this setup plays the same three pairs. Pumps left at 85 and 0: 1760, no collapse, lowest pH 7.35. Pumps at 200 and 100: 9330, no collapse, lowest pH 6.67. Pumps at 200 and 110: 3890, with 7 of 20 collapsed and a lowest pH of 4.10. (1) The concentrate multiplies the production: 100 m3/d of it gives more than five times the methane of the first pair. (2) A good pair of rates and a collapse lie close together. With 110 in place of 100, 7 of 20 digesters collapsed, on day 6 or 7, while they were still starting up. Their acids rose to 52 to 58 kgCOD/m3, the pH settled at 4.1, they made no methane for the rest of the episode, and their net methane was about -8300 afterwards. The 13 others made 9700 with these rates. The seven that collapsed were not weak ones: at 200 and 100 they made more than the other 13. Whether a pair of rates is safe depends on the sludge of the episode. (3) A collapse comes fast, and the digester does not come back. In the collapsed episodes the pH was still at or above 6.5 three decisions before it was below 6.0. Closing the carbohydrate pump or both pumps once the true pH was below 6.0, or turning the carbohydrate pump down to 60 once it was below 6.5, brought no digester back. A program therefore has to act before the pH shows the danger: it has to read the danger from its other readings, or keep a distance from the rates at which a digester collapses. (4) The start is the dangerous part. At 200 and 100 the pumps reach their rates after 2.5 days. The acids then pass through a peak of 4.2 kgCOD/m3 on day 4, because the microorganisms that use them have not yet grown to the new load. The methane outflow rises to about 10600 on day 7 and settles at about 9500 from day 10 on, and the acids are back below 0.5 on day 10 and at 0.2 on day 20. The collapses at 200 and 110 happened in this passage. The start phase of the score covers it: at 200 and 100 its net methane was 8750, and that of each later phase 9480. (5) Fixed rates that came through the start came through the run-out: no digester of these trials collapsed after day 7, and a digester under fixed rates stays where it has settled. This is different for a program that keeps raising the feed: feeding more than a digester bears for good can pay inside the scored days and collapse later, on day 118 or 134 in trials, and the run-out counts such a collapse. (6) The pressure of the gas rises with the production, and at a higher pressure more carbon dioxide stays dissolved, which lowers the pH.

WHAT A PROGRAM DECIDES, AND WHAT IT MAY LEAVE TO THE SEARCH. Everything between the readings and the two rates is the program's choice: which readings it uses, how it combines them over time in its memory, when and how fast it moves each pump in either direction, and how it tells what its own digester bears. It may lower a pump as well as raise it, at any time, and the two pumps need not move together. Nothing here says which of this is right; the trials above held both pumps at fixed rates and say nothing about a program that reads its sensors. The numbers that the strategy does not fix, such as a setpoint, a gain, a threshold, a rate or the size of a step, the program declares as constants with a range, up to 10 of them, and the loop searches better values for them on training episodes before it evaluates the program. The search draws values across the whole of each range, and it ranks a candidate with a failed episode below every candidate without one. So the range of a constant is as wide as the constant keeps its meaning, up to the limits of the pumps where it is a rate. The rates of the trials above are those of pumps that were held fixed after a fast start, and they are no limits for a program that reads its sensors. So a coding agent decides the form of the control, and the search decides the numbers.

RULES FOR A PROGRAM. The benchmark gives a controller no clock, and a program is a controller. The rules of this setup say what that means, and an attempt that breaks one is barred whatever its score.

SEEDS. Every episode of the loop is a training episode of the benchmark. No other controller of this task, its design, its settings or its results, is shown here, and none is a target. Set each new milestone above what this loop's own best program reaches, with no failed episode, and keep raising it.

rules.name: no_clock
rules.text: The program keeps no clock of its own. It does not count its calls of act, the decisions, the days or the laboratory results that have arrived, and it does not add up time, in its memory or anywhere else. Nothing that it does may depend on a value that only tells how far the episode has run, because the task gives a controller no clock: with the length of an episode, a count would tell how many scored decisions are left. What a program keeps from one decision to the next is about the digester, for example earlier readings, averages and trends of them or the sum of its control errors, or about what it has done, for example the rates it asked for or a flag that a phase of its own has ended. A list of the last readings with a fixed largest length is allowed. A list or a number that grows with every decision whatever the digester does is a count and breaks the rule.

rules.name: own_memory
rules.text: The program keeps everything that it remembers in the memory dict that act receives. It keeps nothing in a variable of a module that it changes, in a default argument, in an attribute of a function, in a file or anywhere else outside that dict, so that no episode can learn from another one. Constants of a module that are never changed are allowed.

rules.name: observation_only
rules.text: The observation that act receives is the program's only source about the episode. The program reads no file, no environment variable and no clock of the computer, and it draws no random number, so the same readings always give the same actions. It imports nothing of microbesGYM (mgym_engine, mgym_bench), nothing of the plugin (a1_adm1, bridge) and nothing of soft_control_loop except what a skill of the library needs, and it simulates no model of the digester with a solver.

milestones.name: hold
milestones.description: No evaluation episode failed, and the mean score (net_methane, m3/d) over the evaluation episodes is at least 9277. This is what the fixed rates 200 and 100 m3/d (hold_200_100) scored on the evaluation seeds (9277.5, with no failed episode), so the mark asks for a program that does at least as well. The batch check check_hold in the checks file tests it.
